events.title: The Role of Faith in Human Flourishing
events.description:
What does it truly mean to flourish—and how can societies help people achieve it?

Drawing on groundbreaking data, Dr. Byron Johnson, Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University, will explore the links between faith, well-being, and human flourishing, revealing surprising insights about purpose, relationships, and the pathways to a thriving life. The event will be held at 7pm in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall at Brigham Young University, serving as the opening keynote address of the Religion and Human Flourishing conference.

This lecture is co-sponsored by Wheatley Institute, Brigham Young University's College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences, and College of Religious Education.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER:

Dr. Byron Johnson is the Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University. He is the author of more than 350 journal articles, monographs, and books, focusing much of his professional career on the scientific study of religion, the efficacy of faith-based organizations, and criminal justice. Dr. Johnson is also the project co-director of the Global Flourishing Study. The multi-year data collection and research collaboration has brought researchers from Baylor and Harvard University in partnership with Gallup and the Center for Open Science to gather data from approximately 200,000 participants from 22 countries in order to create an open access resource for researchers, journalists, policymakers, and educators worldwide.

events.description:

events.title: From New Haven to Oslo: What States Do with Religions They'd Rather Not Have
events.description:
This talk will trace what Jehovah’s Witness cases teach about the different approaches to religious freedom on either side of the Atlantic—with American doctrine having grown up around preaching and public speech and recent European cases centering around state recognition.

Josh McDaniel is Assistant Clinical Professor of Law at Harvard Law School and Faculty Director of its Religious Freedom Clinic. A former trial and appellate litigator specializing in First Amendment cases, he earned his BA at Brigham Young University and graduated first in his class from UCLA School of Law.

Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

events.title: Devotional: Rebekka Matheson
events.description:
Rebekka Matheson is an associate professor and course director for the Brain, Behavior, and Movement course in the Department of Preparatory Learning at the BYU School of Medicine. She also serves as the chair of the faculty council of the faculty senate for the school of medicine.

On main campus, she serves as the Associate Director of the Neuroscience Center in the College of Life Sciences, and continues to teach classes for the Neuroscience Center every fall. She co-directs the Neuroscience in Europe International Study Program in spring terms. Matheson graduated from the Neuroscience Center at BYU and then went to medical school at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry, where her clinical and research work emphasized neurology and addiction medicine. While in Rochester, she completed additional graduate coursework in neuropharmacology and physiology. She currently serves in the Relief Society Presidency for the Utah State Hospital branch.

Her remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: 2026 Neal A. Maxwell Lecture
events.description:
The BYU Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship presents its Annual Neal A. Maxwell Lecture, commemorating the Institute’s twentieth anniversary and the centennial of Neal A. Maxwell’s birth. Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will speak on “The Limitless Power of Jesus Christ.”

Elder Renlund was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2015. After earning bachelor’s and medical degrees from the University of Utah, he received medical and research training at Johns Hopkins Hospital. He later served as a professor of medicine at the University of Utah and as medical director of the Utah Transplantation Affiliated Hospitals Cardiac Transplant Program. Elder Renlund was born in Salt Lake City, Utah, in November 1952. He married Ruth Lybbert in 1977. They are the parents of one daughter.

This annual lecture honors Elder Neal A. Maxwell’s legacy of faith and intellect by highlighting scholarship that deepens understanding of the restored gospel.

events.title: Trade, Tariffs, and American's Future
events.description:
Why do tariffs matter—and what do they mean for your future?

Join the Marriott School of Business for a conversation with Ambassador Jamieson Greer, the nation’s top trade negotiator, for an engaging discussion about U.S. trade policy, global business, and America’s role in the world economy.

Bring your questions. Come curious. Leave informed. Refreshments will be served.

Moderated by:
Professor Shad Morris, Marriott School of Business
Professor Cree Jones, J. Reuben Clark Law School

About the SpeakerAmbassador Jamieson Greer serves as the 20th United States Trade Representative and works to advance fair, reciprocal trade, expand markets for American products, and address unfair foreign practices. Previously, he helped shape U.S. trade policy, including negotiations involving China and the USMCA. Aside from a law degree from the University of Virginia and masters degrees from two top universities in Paris, Greer earned a bachelor’s degree in international studies from BYU.

events.description:
Jenny Pulsipher will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is a professor of history at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on early American history, Native American history, nineteenth-century Utah, race, and identity. Pulsipher is known for her award-winning book Swindler Sachem: The American Indian Who Sold His Birthright, Dropped Out of Harvard, and Conned the King of England.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. The restoration is seen for the first time, students and faculty present on the history of the film, and filmmakers and participants often attend to share their insight and experiences.

events.title: Devotional: Bishop L. Todd Budge
events.description:
Bishop L. Todd Budge was named First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric on November 14, 2025. Bishop Budge was sustained as a General Authority Seventy on April 6, 2019, and served in that capacity until his call as Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric in October 2020. Bishop Budge has served in a number of Church callings, including stake president, president of the Japan Tokyo Mission, and Area Seventy.

Bishop Budge received a bachelor of arts degree in economics from BYU in 1984. He worked for Bain & Company Japan; Citibank, N.A.; and GE Capital in both Atlanta and Japan. In 2003 he became president and chief executive officer of Tokyo Star Bank Limited; from 2008 to 2011 he served as chairman of the board. He retired from the bank in 2011. During this time, he also served as a member of the board of directors for Hawaiian Airlines.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Crossing Divides and Preserving Democracy in a Polarized World
events.description:
Join the Wheatley Institute for a conversation with Heather Gerken, president of the Ford Foundation, as she discusses how to effectively navigate polarization and heal divides in order to protect democracy. Her lecture will be held at 7:00pm in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall at Brigham Young University.

Heather Gerken is the 11th president of the Ford Foundation. A nationally recognized expert on democracy, federalism, and elections, Gerken has spent her career working on bipartisan efforts to protect the rule of law.

As president of the Ford Foundation, she leads the $16 billion charitable foundation, which operates offices in the United States and 10 regions around the world.

Sponsored by the Asian Studies program at the Kennedy Center for International Studies.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
events.description:
Elder Ronald A. Rasband was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 3, 2015, after serving as a member of the Presidency of the Seventy since 2005. He has served as a counselor in the Europe Central Area Presidency, president of the Utah Salt Lake City Area, executive director of the Temple Department; and has supervised the North America West, Northwest and three Utah areas as a member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

Elder Rasband attended the University of Utah. In 1987, he was appointed President and Chief Operating Officer of Huntsman Chemical Corporation. When he left Huntsman Chemical Corporation in 1996 to serve as a mission president in New York, he was also serving as a member of the Board of Directors.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.description:

Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, where he focuses on early American religion and culture, revelation, conversion, apostasy, and documentary editing. Harper is known for serving as a managing historian and general editor of Saints and for his work with The Joseph Smith Papers and The Wilford Woodruff Papers.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

events.title: Devotional: Audrey Perry Martin
events.description:
Audrey Perry Martin was appointed assistant to the president for University Communications on June 1, 2025. In this role, she acts as the university’s primary spokesperson and directs the work of BYU University Communications. Perry Martin earned a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center and a bachelor’s degree in political science and journalism from BYU.

Prior to her current role, Perry Martin was a partner at Lex Politica, a national political law firm. Her practice focused on advising corporations, candidates, political committees and parties on campaign and election law issues. Additionally, she worked as counsel for the Committee on House Administration and at the Federal Election Commission.

Her remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Archive Classic Film—The Dead, The Devil, and The Flesh from 1974
events.description:
The Dead, The Devil, and The Flesh (1974) – A professor delves into the study of the dead and the spirit world, eventually delving so deep as to visit as an observer. But such a visit comes with serious consequences.

A film by José Maria Oliveira, a recent convert to the Church in Francoist Spain. Oliveira sought to share his excitement for his new faith through the medium of horror cinema.

A rare screening of a fascinating film from the archives. Restored in 2022.

November 6 7pm BYU Library Auditorium

Join us for this semester’s ARCHIVE CLASSIC – presenting a historical title that has special meaning to the BYU Community.

This film is not currently available outside of BYU, and we plan to screen it about every 4 years.

Don’t miss this singular event!

events.title: Devotional: Elder Joni L. Koch
events.description:
Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch has served in numerous Church callings, including stake president, Area Seventy and president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

Spend an evening with Jeff Flake, Wheatley Fellow and former U.S. ambassador, as he speaks about democracy, responsibility, and citizenship.

The event will be held at 7:00 PM in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER:

Jeff Flake, who is originally from Snowflake, Arizona, has served in a wide number of public positions. His experience in politics include 12 years as a House Representative and six years as a Senator for the state of Arizona, and roughly two and a half years as U.S. Ambassador to the Republic of Türkiye. He is also the founding Director of the Institute of Politics at Arizona State University, Chairman of the Board of World Trade Center Utah, and a non-resident fellow of Wheatley Institute.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

We are happy to present this film for a new audience and restore the history of the work of the BYU Motion Picture Studio.

Starring Gordon Jump and Sherry Brian

November 20 7pm BYU Library Auditorium

Please come celebrate these singular events!

events.title: Devotional: President Timothy L. Farnes
events.description:
President Timothy L. Farnes was sustained as Young Men General President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 5, 2025. He began serving on August 1, 2025. His past Church assignments have included Area Seventy, president of the Brazil São Paulo North Mission and stake president.

President Farnes studied economics at BYU and later founded multiple companies in several industries, as well as a humanitarian nonprofit doing work in Ghana, Africa.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Kimberly Matheson
events.description:
Kimberly Matheson will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is the Laura F. Willes Research Fellow at the Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on Book of Mormon theology, Christian contemplative practice, and the continental philosophy of religion. Matheson is known for authoring Helaman: A Brief Theological Introduction and for her service on the boards of the Book of Mormon Studies Association and the Latter-day Saint Theology Seminar.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
events.description:
Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Creators Club Kickoff
events.description:
Got a business idea? Come find out how to actually get it off the ground.

Join us for the Creators Club kickoff event — a one-hour intro to what Creators Club is all about, what we do, and what's coming this semester, including the Big Idea Competition. We'll also have free food from Sage, Andy Gartz's restaurant in Provo. Before we wrap up, we'll ask you to fill out a quick feedback survey so we can build a semester around what you're most excited to learn.

Here's what to expect after kickoff: every week, a different student speaker will share a real business story in a quick, 10-minute case study — walking through how they took an idea from nothing (level 0) to something real (level 1) through validation. This semester is all about validation — testing your idea before you sink time and money into it. You'll hear directly from students who've used Rollins Center resources, including the Validation Grant, to get their own ideas off the ground.

And here's the fun part: if you make a sale from your business anytime this semester, you're invited to an exclusive end-of-semester dinner — gourmet pizza, made by Sage.

events.title: Utah Entrepreneur Challenge Application Deadline
events.description:
The Tim Draper Utah Entrepreneur Challenge (UEC) is a statewide, student business competition. Teams from universities across Utah compete for the best student business and a chance to win cash and prizes. We invite all students in Utah from participating colleges and universities to apply. The challenge will culminate with at a final event at the University of Utah. Participating teams are judged by industry professionals, experienced entrepreneurs and community experts. Judges will allocate $75,000 in prizes and awards to the top 20 finalists. Many past winners have developed into successful enterprises. The program is managed by the Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute at the University of Utah. Sponsors include Tim Draper, a renowned venture capitalist.

https://lassonde.utah.edu/uec/apply/

events.description:
D. Brett Pennington (BS '94) is a senior energy executive with nearly 30 years of leadership and technical experience in the oil and gas industry. He currently serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Ensign Natural Resources, a private equity-backed exploration and production company focused on the acquisition, development and optimization of oil and gas assets. Under his leadership, Ensign acquired a 130,000-acre position and built a management and operating organization of over 140 employees. The company transformed the asset in just three years before selling to Marathon Oil for approximately $3 billion.

Prior to Ensign, Mr. Pennington held senior executive positions with Murphy Oil Corporation and spent more than a decade with ExxonMobil in engineering, planning, project management, and leadership roles. Mr. Pennington serves on the Board of Directors of the Texas Oil & Gas Association. He holds a bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering from Brigham Young University and completed the Advanced Management Program at Harvard Business School, along with executive programs at Wharton and Thunderbird.

events.title: Career in Math Talk: Sabrina Smith (Quant at GS)
Colloquium: Sebastian Acosta (Baylor College of Medicine)
events.description:
Title: Mathematics of nonlinear ultrasound imaging: Advances and open problems.

Abstract: The Westervelt equation models the propagation of high-intensity ultrasound waves. For medical imaging purposes, it is needed to estimate the parameters in the equation that model wave speed, diffusivity, and nonlinearity. I will discuss up to date progress on this problem, as well as open questions, from the mathematical point of view. I will also present our contribution which shows that by using time-periodic solutions excited from the boundary at a sufficiently high frequency, knowledge of the first- and second-harmonic Cauchy data at the boundary is sufficient to simultaneously determine the wave speed, diffusivity and nonlinearity in the interior of the domain of interest.

events.title: From New Haven to Oslo: What States Do with Religions They'd Rather Not Have
events.description:
This talk will trace what Jehovah’s Witness cases teach about the different approaches to religious freedom on either side of the Atlantic—with American doctrine having grown up around preaching and public speech and recent European cases centering around state recognition.
Josh McDaniel is Assistant Clinical Professor of Law at Harvard Law School and Faculty Director of its Religious Freedom Clinic. A former trial and appellate litigator specializing in First Amendment cases, he earned his BA at Brigham Young University and graduated first in his class from UCLA School of Law.
Part of our fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

events.title: Joy in the Journey: Learn, Grow, Serve
events.description:
The Kennedy Center's 2026 honored alum is Jeremy Andrus. Come hear him deliver his Honored Alumni Lecture at the Kennedy Center, part of Homecoming Week!
Jeremy Andrus (BS '96, MBA ’02) is President and CEO of Traeger Grills, the wood pellet grill brand. He and a financial partner acquired the company in 2014, transforming it from a small, regional, business into a multi-hundred-million-dollar brand that owns over 50% of the global wood pellet grill market.
While Traeger has become Jeremy’s most successful business story, it isn’t his first. He joined the start-up Skullcandy in 2005 with 4 employees and less than $1m in sales. Under his leadership, the headphone company transformed into a $300 million brand. Jeremy was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year in 2016, Mountain West Capital Network Utah Entrepreneur of the Year in 2017, and was inducted into the Utah Technology Council Hall of Fame in 2018. He serves on the board of directors of World Trade Center Utah, GOED, Silicon Slopes, and Utah Olympic Legacy Foundation. Jeremy received his MBA from Harvard Business School and BA from Brigham Young University. He lives in Salt Lake City with his wife Kristin and their six children.
